contour.name: Customer inquiry and service request
contour.scope: External inquiry, service request, communications and resolution. Incident/problem/work remain separate authorities.
invariants: A case has a requester or an explicit anonymous mode.
Repeated inquiries may be merged or related without losing chronology.
Many cases may reference one incident or root-cause fix.
Resolution, closure and customer acceptance are distinct assertions.
contour.decision: Choose REUSE ONLY, PROFILE, or NEW MODEL. Prefer reuse and do not create a duplicate aggregate.

model.name: Service Case / Ticket
model.purpose: Represent a governed request, inquiry, issue or complaint that an organization receives, owns, coordinates and brings to an evidence-backed outcome across channels and systems.
model.scope_statement: Owns case identity, classification, participation roles, intake, triage, case state, assignment, case-local communication and evidence indexes, applied commitment instances, outcome, closure, reopening and governed projections while referencing external parties, content, policies and work execution.
in_scope: Case identity, intake, classification, relationships, requester and handling roles, state and assignment history
Case-local communication, evidence and knowledge bindings, applied service commitments, outcome, closure, feedback and federation
Typed references to parties, products, services, contracts, messages, documents, tasks, policies, calendars and knowledge
out_of_scope: Person or organization identity, message and document payloads, generic workflow, work-order execution, knowledge lifecycle and policy evaluation engines
Universal status, priority, entitlement, SLA, complaint, resolution or retention vocabularies
Access enforcement, audit-log persistence and master data owned by external systems

boundary_notes.distinction: These are profile-bound case types. A complaint may follow ISO 10002, but that complaints profile does not define every service case.
A case is a handling aggregate initiated around a need or issue; the underlying incident, defect, problem or affected object keeps its own identity and lifecycle.
The case owns coordination status and assignments but references independently governed execution tasks and workflows.
The case stores the pinned policy binding and observed KPI timer instance, while policy definition and business-time calculation remain external.
The case indexes relevance, chronology and visibility; external systems own message, file, evidence and knowledge payload lifecycles.

composition.purpose: Binds requester, submitter, beneficiary, owner, assignee and collaborator identities without duplicating their master records.

composition.target: Product, Service, Asset and Entitlement models
composition.purpose: Identifies the supported or affected object and coverage authority without importing those lifecycles.
Maintains case chronology, participant and visibility bindings while the communication system owns content and delivery records.
Indexes case evidence with integrity, provenance and access bindings while the repository owns content and custody.

composition.target: Task, Work Order and Workflow models
composition.purpose: Links executable work without conflating case state with task completion or resource allocation.

composition.target: SLA Policy and Business Calendar models
composition.purpose: Pins policy, KPI and calendar versions used to calculate case commitment instances.
Binds suggested or applied knowledge with version and applicability without owning article publication.

composition.target: Jira issue and Zendesk ticket schemas
composition.purpose: Supports versioned import and export mappings with explicit loss and extension handling.
Aligns case entities, revisions, activities and accountable agents for portable provenance.

providerPolicy.scope: Canonical single-stream subject-model research after the six-workstream consolidation

waived_providers.reason: Claude produced no result on prior 1800-second and 900-second attempts and again timed out on bounded 600-second Sonnet and 300-second Haiku passes. The owner prioritized completion over provider availability.

The repository owner authorized completion without Grok when Grok is unavailable, slow or schema-invalid. Grok may still be attempted as a bounded supplemental reviewer, but its failure never blocks a valid Claude plus no-tools result.

providerPolicy.review_rule: Codex may complete source-grounded fallback research after bounded Claude and Grok attempts fail. It requires a separate no-tools adversarial audit and remains reviewable-draft with a visible absence-of-external-review hold.

supplemental_provider_attempts.admission_rule: Use only a locally schema-valid result whose sources and boundaries survive adjudication.
Use only a locally schema-valid result whose sources and boundaries survive adjudication.

boundaryDecision.rationale: The record-plane label standalone-mm is separate from subject kind. A service case groups intake, evolving decisions, role bindings, communications, evidence references, commitments and outcomes under one governed identity, so aggregate is more defensible than entity or event.

decisions.rationale: Request, inquiry, issue and complaint are represented as profile-bound case classifications. The base model does not force complaint-specific or vendor-specific semantics on every case.
The case handles a need or reported condition but references the originating incident, problem, product, service or asset, which retains independent identity and lifecycle.
Case assignment and coordination are native, while tasks, work orders and workflows remain independently governed and are linked by reference.
These roles can belong to different identities and have different authority, privacy and communication consequences, so they cannot be collapsed into one customer field.
Platform and organization vocabularies are not semantically identical. Every case pins the applicable profile and preserves original external codes during federation.

decisions.disposition: accepted as binding and observed instance only
decisions.rationale: The case records which entitlement, policy, KPI and calendar were applied and the resulting target, pause and breach observations, while policy design and time calculation remain external.
A resolved status does not prove requester acceptance, factual correction, regulatory compliance or completed downstream work. Each assertion retains its own authority and evidence.
The case owns chronology, relevance and visibility bindings while message, document, evidence and knowledge systems retain payload mastership and lifecycle.

decisions.disposition: not applicable to the case aggregate
decisions.rationale: A service case is an abstract aggregate. Physical properties belong to referenced affected objects, while case-local descriptive, temporal, relational and outcome properties remain native.
Append-only revisions, authority, ETag or equivalent concurrency, pinned mappings and explicit transform loss are required because cases are mutable and commonly synchronized across systems.

Every finding asks for current governed value, source and temporal provenance, and authorized revision or conflict handling. Repeated structure is machine-friendly but still needs later sector-profile editorial review.

publicationHolds: Claude and Grok timed out during their bounded attempts, so independent external review is absent and explicitly waived for this published reviewable draft.
The shared relation ledger contains no approved outgoing edges for WM-ACT-021, so all sibling-model links in this draft are provisional composition proposals until registry reconciliation.

Clause and field-level mappings, exact external schema versions and round-trip behavior remain unverified for canonical conformance even though official source pages were checked during Codex research.
Sector and jurisdiction profiles must validate case types, status vocabularies, service commitments, closure, privacy and retention rules before operational enforcement.
Independent external review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this codex-only result remains a reviewable draft.
deferredResearch: Validate the logical structure against public service, healthcare, finance, education, legal, employment, facilities, IT service management and customer-support case profiles.
Create clause and field-level crosswalks for ISO 10002, Jira, Zendesk, Dynamics 365 and additional portable case-management schemas.
Approve sibling model identifiers, relation directions and cardinality contracts for parties, products, services, communications, evidence, work, policies, calendars and knowledge.
Review generated question wording with case workers, service agents, records managers, privacy officers and platform architects.

functions.name: Register case
functions.description: Create a case from an authorized submission without inventing missing facts.
preconditions: intake purpose and record authority are known
effects: an attributable case with explicit unknowns exists

functions.name: Validate and triage case
functions.description: Check minimum data, duplicates, scope, eligibility and routing rules.
effects: acceptance, rejection or redirect is preserved with rationale

functions.name: Classify and prioritize case
functions.description: Apply pinned type, category, impact, urgency and priority schemes.
effects: routing inputs are reproducible without a universal vocabulary

functions.name: Link or merge case
functions.description: Create a typed case relation or merge a duplicate while preserving aliases.
preconditions: identities resolve and merge policy permits the action
effects: predecessor identities and history remain resolvable

functions.name: Assign or route case
functions.description: Bind or change the accountable owner, queue and working assignee.
preconditions: target is eligible and actor is authorized
effects: current assignment and full routing history are distinguishable

functions.name: Transition case state
functions.description: Apply a permitted state transition with reason and effective time.
preconditions: transition profile and authority permit the change
effects: case state changes without rewriting prior revisions

functions.name: Record case communication
functions.description: Link a message or delivery event with audience and visibility metadata.
effects: chronology is updated while the message system retains mastership

functions.name: Bind evidence or knowledge
functions.description: Attach a governed reference to evidence, a document or knowledge item.
preconditions: reference resolves and access is allowed
effects: case context expands without copying the external lifecycle

functions.name: Evaluate case commitment
functions.description: Record case-bound SLA KPI timing using external policy and calendar results.
preconditions: policy, KPI and calendar versions resolve
effects: target, pause and breach status are reproducible

functions.name: Resolve, close or cancel case
functions.description: Record an authorized outcome and completion decision separately.
preconditions: state profile and authority permit the action
effects: resolution, acceptance, closure and cancellation remain distinct

functions.name: Reopen or appeal case
functions.description: Create a governed continuation from new evidence, failed outcome or appeal.
effects: prior outcome remains immutable and linked

functions.name: Issue case projection
functions.description: Produce a minimum authorized view for a recipient, purpose or external schema.
effects: redaction, mapping version and provenance are recorded

model.name: Work Order
model.purpose: Represent an authoritative, versioned instruction that authorizes and constrains one or more units of work while preserving boundaries to requests, procedures, schedules and performed-work evidence.
model.scope_statement: Owns order identity, authorization, scope, requirements, administrative lifecycle, change control, acceptance criteria and closure disposition; references execution and domain records governed elsewhere.
in_scope: Order identity, class, authority, scope, requirements, constraints and order-level planning commitments
Administrative state transitions, revisions, cancellation, acceptance decision, closure and governance metadata
Typed references to tasks, procedures, targets, resources, contracts, schedules and performed-work evidence
out_of_scope: Task execution semantics, detailed scheduling, inventory transactions, cost accounting, access enforcement and proof that physical work occurred
Lifecycle ownership of referenced assets, people, organizations, locations, contracts, procedures or evidence records

boundary_notes.distinction: A request proposes or demands work and can be rejected; a work order is an authorized instruction with controlled scope and lifecycle.
The order may contain task references and pin procedure versions, but task execution semantics and reusable instructions remain in their own models.
A work order authorizes work; performed-work records and evidence establish what actually happened and are only referenced here.
The order may carry windows and commitments, but resource-level sequencing and calendar optimization belong to a schedule model.

composition.purpose: Groups typed task references and order-local parameters without claiming ownership of task execution semantics.
Pins the executable instruction version while keeping reusable procedure content outside the order.
Delegates detailed sequencing and capacity allocation while retaining order-level timing commitments.

composition.target: Asset, location, person, organization, material and inventory models
composition.purpose: Uses authoritative domain identities without copying their properties or lifecycles.
Binds governing agreements and commercial limits without turning the order into a ledger.
Separates authorization from claims and proof of actual execution.

composition.target: ISA-95, OPC UA ISA-95, PLCS and UN/EDIFACT concepts
composition.purpose: Maintains documented semantic mappings without claiming conformance to any one implementation profile.

model.name: Communication Interaction
model.purpose: Provide the format-neutral context an agent needs to open, conduct, evidence, classify, correlate and close a communication interaction - a bounded exchange of contact turns between identified parties across one or more channels - with its participant roster, channel and endpoint bindings, turn content, delivery evidence, lifecycle state, outcome and governance references.
model.scope_statement: WM-ACT-027 models the interaction record as an aggregate: an interaction root carrying identity, classification, participants-in-role, channel and endpoint bindings, ordered turns with content and attachments, threading relations, lifecycle and handling state, temporal points and windows, delivery and engagement evidence, outcome/disposition, and typed references to the party, permission, access, retention and audit models that own their own semantics. It stops at transport protocols, party master data, permission evaluation, policy enforcement, audit-trail production and disposition execution. It is storage- and interface-neutral: JSON, YAML, Markdown, HTML, Git, MCP and MongoDB are projections of these semantics, not their definition.
in_scope: The interaction as a unit of account: what opens one, what continues it across a channel switch, what closes it
Interaction identity, correlation keys and cross-channel identifier resolution
Participants in roles (initiator, addressee, copied, observer, handler) as references into an external party model
Channel classification, channel capability constraints, and endpoint/address bindings including proxy-address pairs
Direction (inbound, outbound, internal) and initiation attribution
Ordered turns with authorship, sequence, content references and attachments
Threading, reply and relation structure between turns and between interactions
Lifecycle and handling state, assignment of handling responsibility, and state-change reasons
Interaction time points, periods and channel engagement windows/timers
Delivery, receipt, read and engagement evidence attached to turns
Capture provenance: which system observed or authored the record and how faithfully
Outcome, resolution and wrap-up disposition of the interaction
Confidentiality/visibility classification and redaction markers carried on the record
References to permission basis, retention class, access policy and audit records owned by sibling models
Alignment bindings to external interaction schemas and vocabularies
out_of_scope: Party, organisation and person master data and their identity lifecycle (owned by the party model)
The canonical contact-point/electronic-address registry and address verification
Permission and consent capture, evaluation and withdrawal semantics (this model carries only a reference to the decision)
Runtime access-control evaluation and enforcement (this model carries classification markers only)
Audit-trail creation, immutability guarantees and audit query semantics
Execution of deletion, anonymisation or disposition (this model carries the class and a tombstone marker only)
Transport and signalling protocol behaviour (SIP/IMS sessions, SMTP relay, SMS submission, charging/CDR production)
Case, ticket, order or service-request lifecycle (referenced, not reproduced)
Campaign, journey and outbound orchestration logic
Bot/NLU intent model training, ranking and dialogue policy
Media file storage, transcoding and CDN delivery
Workforce management, agent scheduling and staffing forecasts
Billing, rating and settlement for communication traffic

boundary_notes.neighbor: Party / party-role model (e.g. TM Forum TMF632/TMF669 pattern)
boundary_notes.distinction: TMF683 carries only relatedParty references with a role; the interaction record must not restate party attributes, party identity resolution or party lifecycle.

ePrivacy and 47 CFR 64.1200 place consent capture, validity and revocation with the permission holder; this model records only the reference to a permission decision that was in force at send time, never the evaluation.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Clinical or business request model (FHIR CommunicationRequest)
boundary_notes.distinction: FHIR separates the planned/ordered communication from the record of one that occurred; WM-ACT-027 covers the occurrence, with the request kept as a basedOn reference.
FHIR explicitly distinguishes Communication from AuditEvent; system-level disclosure tracking and audit-trail semantics stay in the audit model.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Transport and protocol layer (RFC 5322 trace fields, Matrix federation, carrier submission)
boundary_notes.distinction: Trace/Received fields and protocol event graphs are informational transport artefacts; this model consumes their identifiers and status outcomes without owning routing or delivery mechanics.

Sector rules such as MiFID II impose fixed retention on communication records, but the retention schedule and its execution belong to the retention model; this record only binds a retention class and a disposition marker.
Attachment bytes, transcoding and storage location are owned by the content model; this model carries attachment references, media type and integrity digests.

composition.purpose: Registers Communication Interaction as a specialisation of the parent activity concept, inheriting generic activity identity and actor structure rather than restating it.
Participants are carried as party references with a role, mirroring the TMF683 relatedParty pattern; party attributes, identity resolution and lifecycle remain with the party model.

composition.target: Contact point and electronic address registry model
composition.purpose: Endpoint bindings cite canonical contact points; address verification, reachability and ownership stay in the registry.
Channel codes and capability constraints are dereferenced from the channel registry so that channel definitions are not duplicated per interaction.
Carries only a decision reference and point-in-time basis snapshot; capture, evaluation, validity and withdrawal of permission are owned entirely by that model.
Provides based-on and part-of links so an interaction can be situated in a wider work item without importing that item's lifecycle.
Attachment and recording bytes, storage location and transcoding are owned by the content model; this model holds references, media types and digests.
Supplies the retention class, schedule and disposition execution; this model contributes only the trigger time, hold marker and tombstone shape.
Consumes the confidentiality and redaction markers carried here; evaluation and enforcement of access requests are never performed by this model.

composition.target: Audit trail and event log model
composition.purpose: Receives access and change events concerning interaction records; FHIR's explicit Communication-versus-AuditEvent split keeps audit-trail semantics outside this boundary.
Supplies the shared pattern for authoritative identifier, alias retention, superseded-by links and correlation keys used across the interaction root, turns and artifacts.
Binds all recorded time points to the RFC 3339 profile including seconds, explicit offset and the unknown-offset convention.

composition.target: TM Forum TMF683 Party Interaction resource
composition.purpose: Element-level alignment for direction, status, channel, interactionDate, interactionItem, relatedParty, note and interactionRelationship, recorded as alignment with conflicts noted rather than a conformance claim.
Alignment for status, category, medium, sender, recipient, sent, received, payload, inResponseTo and about in healthcare-facing deployments, without adopting FHIR's clinical context model.
Alignment for actor, object, target, audience targeting and inReplyTo when interactions are projected into social or federated activity feeds.
Consumes measure definitions and derived durations declared here and extends them into aggregate reporting; aggregation, benchmarking and visualisation are not modelled locally.

model.name: Issue / Problem
model.purpose: Give an agent the format-neutral context needed to recognize, record, classify, analyse, relate, govern and hand off a recognized discrepancy between an observed state and a required or expected state, without owning the work, change, enforcement or audit trail that resolves it.
model.scope_statement: An Issue / Problem record asserts that some observed state of a subject diverges from a stated expectation (requirement, specification, norm, target or design intent) and that the divergence is recognized as needing disposition. The model covers the discrepancy assertion itself, its identity, classification and grading, its recognition context in time and place, its evidence and provenance, its impact and causal analysis, its lifecycle states and disposition, its relationships to other issues and subjects, and the governance, confidentiality, assurance and retention context of the record. It deliberately stops at the boundary of the work: corrective and preventive actions, changes, incident response execution, verification execution, enforcement and audit trails are referenced, never reproduced. The model is storage- and interface-neutral: tracker rows, occurrence databases, nonconformance reports, SARIF results, Markdown files and MongoDB documents are projections of the same semantics.
in_scope: Assertion of a discrepancy: observed state, expected state and the reference norm or requirement against which the divergence is judged
Identity of the issue record, duplicate resolution, merge/canonical selection and correspondence with identifiers in other systems
Typology and grading: issue type, category codes, severity, priority, urgency and assessed impact
Recognition context: who or what detected the discrepancy, through which channel, under which environment and configuration
Separated time anchors for occurrence, detection, report submission and record ingestion
Evidence set, reproducibility and the provenance and confidence of every asserted claim on the record
Extent of impact, affected subjects, occurrence aggregation and recurrence semantics
Causal analysis outcomes: hypothesis, proximate and root cause, contributing factors, and known-error designation
Documented workaround and mitigation knowledge held as knowledge, not as executed work
Lifecycle states, permitted transitions, triage acceptance, disposition categories and closure criteria
Relationships between issues and to incidents, requirements, assets, tests, actions and changes
Governance context: accountable roles, competent decision authority, waiver/concession reference, sensitivity, reporter protection, retention class and hold status
Interoperability crosswalks to external issue, defect, nonconformance and occurrence vocabularies
out_of_scope: Execution, scheduling and tracking of corrective, preventive or containment actions, which belong to the action/work model referenced as parent WM-ACT-021
Change request implementation and release semantics, which belong to a change model aligned to OSLC Change Management
Incident detection, triage and response operations, which belong to an incident/occurrence model
Risk identification, analysis and treatment for events that have not been realized
Runtime evaluation or enforcement of validation rules, routing rules or policy: this model declares constraints, an external evaluator or engine applies them
Audit-trail generation and retention of who did what to the record, which belongs to the adopting Dimension's audit-log service
Governance of classification schemes, taxonomies and code lists themselves (for example ADREP/ECCAIRS, CWE); this model binds to them
Verification and validation execution proving an action was effective; only the reference and acceptance status are carried
Physical or logical deletion execution and destruction certification, which belongs to a records retention and disposition model
Party, organization and role master data
Specification, requirement and norm authoring and versioning
Security vulnerability enumeration, scoring and coordinated disclosure workflow, which is a specialized sibling model

boundary_notes.distinction: An incident is an unplanned event or interruption that occurred at a point in time; an issue is the recognized discrepancy that one or more incidents may evidence. NIST SP 800-61r3 scopes incident response as an operational cycle inside cybersecurity risk management, and Regulation (EU) No 376/2014 treats an occurrence report as an event record with its own transmission deadlines. The issue record references occurrences; it does not carry their response lifecycle.

A risk is an unrealized possibility carried for treatment; an issue is a recognized, already-observed divergence. Regulation (EU) No 376/2014 applies a safety risk classification to occurrences that have already happened, which shows risk scoring can be an attribute of an issue without making the issue a risk. Forward-looking likelihood modelling stays in the risk model.

21 CFR 820.100 separates investigating the cause of nonconformities from identifying, implementing and verifying the action. The issue owns the discrepancy, the investigation outcome and the disposition decision context; the action model owns action definition, execution and effectiveness verification. The issue carries only the reference and the acceptance status.

OSLC Change Management models ChangeRequest, Task and ReviewTask as trackable executable activities with their own state predicates. Assignment, effort, scheduling and workflow execution belong there. This model retains the discrepancy semantics and links to the change request rather than duplicating its workflow.

The expected state that makes a discrepancy a discrepancy is authored and versioned elsewhere. The issue carries a resolvable reference to the norm clause and the norm version in force at recognition time, not the norm text.

Tool runs, logs, samples, images and measurement results are entities with their own provenance. SARIF models a result inside a run with its own artifact and provenance objects. The issue references evidence and states its sufficiency; it does not become the evidence store.

A vulnerability is a specialized weakness class with registry-governed identifiers, scoring systems and coordinated disclosure states. It behaves as a specialization of an issue but carries machinery this generic model must not absorb; SARIF keeps taxonomy membership in taxa references rather than in the result itself.

Regulation (EU) No 376/2014 places retention, de-identification and repository transfer duties on designated bodies. This model declares the retention class, hold state and tombstone marker on its own records but does not own destruction execution or certification.

ADREP/ECCAIRS compatibility is mandated for aviation occurrence systems and SARIF results point at external taxa. Code list governance, versioning and deprecation stay in the classifier registry; the issue binds a code plus the scheme identifier and version.

21 CFR 820.100 lists complaints as one of several quality data sources analysed to detect nonconformities. A complaint is an intake channel artifact; it may cause an issue to be registered but is not itself the issue.

composition.purpose: Registered parent in the action plane. The issue is the recognized discrepancy that motivates action; the parent owns action definition, assignment, scheduling, effort and execution. This model contributes the discrepancy, causal and disposition context and receives back only references and acceptance status. 21 CFR 820.100 separates investigating the cause from identifying, implementing and verifying the action, and OSLC CM keeps Task and ReviewTask as separate trackable activities.

Carry references to the occurrences an issue explains, with the explanatory role and, where required, the onward-transmission obligation. The occurrence record's own detection, response and closure lifecycle stays entirely in that model.

Bind a realized risk to the issue it became, and carry an endorsed risk classification value assigned to the discrepancy. Likelihood modelling, treatment planning and risk-appetite evaluation remain with the risk model.
Resolve the expected state against an authored requirement clause at the version in force at recognition. Requirement authoring, versioning and baseline control stay with that model.

Reference corrections, corrective actions and preventive actions with their roles, and the effectiveness verification or validation results they produce. Action execution and the verification activity itself are owned there; this model carries only the reference and the resulting acceptance status.

composition.target: Change request model aligned to OSLC Change Management 3.0
composition.purpose: Align state, priority, severity, parent and related-request semantics to the oslc_cm vocabulary for exchange, using oslc_cm:state in preference to the archaic oslc_cm:status. Alignment only: no conformance is claimed and change workflow is not reproduced.
Reference evidence items with custodian, capture time and content digest, and reproduction procedures. Evidence capture, storage and integrity verification remain with that model.

composition.target: Provenance model aligned to W3C PROV-O
composition.purpose: Express per-claim attribution, derivation of merged and superseded records, and assertion intervals using the PROV Entity/Activity/Agent pattern and its qualification classes.

Bind category codes to externally governed schemes with an explicit scheme identifier and version, as ADREP/ECCAIRS compatibility and SARIF taxa references both require. Code list governance, deprecation and versioning stay in the registry.
Resolve reporter, owner, custodian, analyst, competent authority and recipient references. Party master data, role definitions and competence assertions are owned there.

composition.target: Records retention and disposition policy model
composition.purpose: Bind the retention class, anchor and hold authority, and receive the disposal authorisation reference. Schedule authoring, destruction execution and disposal certification are owned by that model or by the adopting Dimension's policy.

composition.target: Audit log service of the adopting Dimension
composition.purpose: Reference the externally generated audit trail of who read or modified the issue record. This model declares what must be logged; generation, immutability and retention of the audit trail are owned entirely by that service and are not audit semantics of this model.

Reference specialized weakness records that behave as issues but carry registry-governed identifiers, scoring systems and coordinated disclosure states. Those states and scoring machinery are not reproduced here.

Apply a shared sensitivity, de-identification and release-condition vocabulary to the issue record, its evidence and its derived extracts, so that classification semantics are common across record types rather than redefined per model.
